sources.entry: pyyaml - A full-featured YAML framework for Python.

summary.one_liner: PyYAML is a full-featured YAML processing framework for Python, with optional fast LibYAML-based parser and emitter bindings.
summary.what_it_does: Provides YAML loading and dumping for Python via yaml.load and yaml.dump, with a safe_load option for untrusted input. The setup script detects whether LibYAML is installed and, if so, builds bindings that let you use CLoader and CDumper for faster parsing and emitting. You can force or skip the LibYAML build with the --with-libyaml and --without-libyaml setup options. The README describes a Makefile-based test suite that runs pure Python tests and LibYAML extension tests, with the LibYAML version pinned by LIBYAML-REF (default 0.2.5). Further references point to a homepage, tutorial, reference docs, a Matrix/IRC channel, and a bug tracker.
use_cases: parse YAML config files in Python
serialize Python data structures to YAML
speed up YAML parsing with LibYAML
read and write YAML settings or manifests
notable: Optional LibYAML-based CLoader and CDumper for faster parsing and emitting
safe_load function for untrusted YAML input
Makefile test targets for pure Python and LibYAML modes
Pinned LibYAML build version via LIBYAML-REF
caveats: Installation uses setup.py directly; the README does not mention pip packaging
LibYAML bindings are optional and only used when LibYAML is installed or explicitly enabled
Full test suite depends on make and building a local copy of LibYAML
